clue.text: Look of distinguished person in confrontation

definitions.note: the answer is the noun use, a face-to-face being a meeting in person

parts.note: to face is to look towards, and a face is also a look or expression
the two prepositions swap in phrases such as 'the key of the door'
a famous face is a well-known, notable person

explanation.surface: Someone eminent glares at an opponent during a heated standoff.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: the same word is used twice, once as a look and once as a celebrity, joined by a preposition.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting held in person, with both parties present and opposite each other, is called this, especially a tense one.

clue.text: Physically weak female bird

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
a rail is a marsh bird, like the water rail

explanation.surface: A description of a weak, sickly hen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frail is delicate in body, lacking strength through age or illness.

clue.text: Fail to reach a hairdresser?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for failing badly or falling heavily
second meaning, whimsical: arrive at someone who crops hair

explanation.surface: Someone never makes it to their haircut appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading, where a cropper is taken literally as one who crops hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to suffer a sudden failure or heavy fall, originally from riders thrown head first.

clue.text: Designate period of time in office

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to name or call something
second meaning: the span an official serves

explanation.surface: Assigning how long someone will hold a post.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to name or label; as a noun it is the fixed tenure of an elected official.

clue.text: One who doesn't eat in a more hurried manner

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person going without food
second meaning: the comparative of quick

explanation.surface: Someone skipping meals rushes around more than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A person abstaining from food is a faster; the comparative adverb of quick shares the same spelling.

clue.text: Come together, heading for collision on side of road

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
a verge is the grass strip along the edge of a road

explanation.surface: Two cars meet, one about to crash on the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines or groups that converge meet at a single point, moving towards each other.

clue.text: Interjection, say, in wedding day toast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a grammatical category, of which an interjection is one example
second meaning, whimsical: a portion of an address given at a reception

explanation.surface: Someone shouts out during the best man's speech at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the interjection as an example; the question mark flags the literal second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar sorts words into classes such as noun, verb and interjection, each called by this name.

clue.text: Pure Charlie and speed

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
haste is speed or hurry
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: An odd pairing of virtue with a man named Charlie and the drug speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone chaste is virtuous and abstains from sex, hence morally unsullied.

clue.text: Respects one crushed by broken dreams

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces that can be reassembled in a new order
being crushed by something means being squeezed inside it, surrounded on both sides

parts.note: the letters rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone whose hopes have been shattered still holds others in esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with approval and esteem, close to respecting them.

clue.text: Tidy hospital somewhere in Wales

parts.note: neat means tidy or orderly
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A clean, well-kept hospital in a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a market town in south Wales, near Swansea, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: What bank may offer only over the phone

indicators.note: a phone carries only voices, so the word is judged by how it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: lone means single or only

explanation.surface: A bank's credit offered by telephone only.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks lend money to customers as a sum to be repaid with interest.

clue.text: Ten memos distributed as reminders

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around and scattered, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the eight letters, taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: An office sends round ten notes to jog people's memories.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvenirs and keepsakes kept to recall people or events are reminders of them.

clue.text: New and strangely serious obsession

indicators.note: acting strangely means behaving out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh and oddly grave fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety, often showing as a compulsive fixation.

clue.text: Boat, say, overturned on offshore ridge

parts.note: a bar is a sandbank or ridge across a harbour mouth

indicators.note: something overturned is flipped upside down, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which 'say' also signals

explanation.surface: A vessel capsizes on a sandbank out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The capsizing boat picture hides that 'Boat' is the definition and 'say' is the piece being flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a flat-bottomed vessel used on canals and rivers for carrying freight.

clue.text: Disinfect top of bacteria-ridden drain

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so just the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter
to leach is to drain away, as liquid through soil

explanation.surface: Cleaning the grimy plughole of a germ-filled sink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine-based whitener is used to kill germs, so to apply it is to sterilise or sanitise.

clue.text: Howler made by boss endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: An embarrassing blunder by the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring, embarrassing mistake, which is exactly what a social blunder is.

clue.text: Fires? It's time for us to leave!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: dismisses an employee, releases them

definitions.text: It's time for us to leave!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a call to depart together

explanation.surface: Someone spots flames and urges everyone to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as a verb phrase with an apostrophe-free 'lets': the employer releases a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An employer who dismisses staff releases them; and the phrase is a common rallying call meaning we should depart now.

clue.text: Former hotel employee — one with dealings abroad

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a porter carries guests' luggage in a hotel

explanation.surface: A one-time hotel worker who now trades internationally.
explanation.definitionFit: A company or trader that sells goods to foreign countries does business overseas.

clue.text: Copies of recordings without the intro

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so dropping it removes the first letter

parts.note: tapes are recordings on magnetic tape

explanation.surface: Bootleg duplicates of music tracks with the opening cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or mimic them, so the verb means copies.

clue.text: Piece of baked Alaska served up as part of meal?

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
a piece is a portion, so the letters lie within the run of words

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A slice of a classic meringue dessert served at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Baked Alaska is ice cream inside meringue, browned in the oven; the dessert is a decoy for the course hidden backwards inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of mixed leaves and vegetables is commonly one course or side of a dinner.

clue.text: Soldier possibly beginning to injure opponent

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant; 'possibly' marks it as an example

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A soldier starts to hurt his enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who opposes a policy or cause, so is an opponent of it.

clue.text: Somewhat animalistic, he's self-motivated for the mating game?

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following words is used

parts.note: letters across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A lusty man, driven by his own urges, playing the dating game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests romance, but mate is the winning move in this board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game ends with checkmate, so it is playfully described as a game of mating.

clue.text: Fish also found in extremely sizeable eastern lake

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another
at its extremes means only the two end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
also and 'and' both add something further
E is the abbreviation for eastern
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in a big lake in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand eel is a small slender fish that burrows in sand, food for puffins.

clue.text: And so, is the travelling staggered?

indicators.note: things travelling move about and change position, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters, taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the person on the move wobbled on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' looks like a word about tottering while walking; it is the definition in its sense of amazed.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered here means stunned with surprise, a synonym of amazed or flabbergasted.
